# Collections

Import, export, and edit the beatmap collections stored in Realm.

## export-collection

Writes one collection, or all of them, to the legacy `collections.db` format.

[Full source](https://github.com/heyngra/osu-files/blob/main/examples/export-collection/index.js)

```sh
cd examples/export-collection
npm install
npm start
```

Open Realm in read-only mode. Exporting does not need a write transaction.

<GuideSource source="examples/export-collection/index.js" :start-line="30" :end-line="30">

```js
const initialized = init(osuLazerRealmPath, { readOnly: true })
```

</GuideSource>

The collection module returns detached snapshots. Reading `.get` here loads every collection.

<GuideSource source="examples/export-collection/index.js" :start-line="39" :end-line="39">

```js
const all = initialized.collections.get
```

</GuideSource>

Enter `all` to export every collection, or type an exact name to export one. Name lookup returns the first matching snapshot.

<GuideSource source="examples/export-collection/index.js" :start-line="60" :end-line="72">

```js
let data
if (choice.toLowerCase() === 'all') {
  data = initialized.collections.exportLegacy(all)
  console.log(`  Exporting all ${all.length} collections`)
} else {
  const found = initialized.collections.get.byName(choice).first()
  if (!found) {
    console.log(`Collection '${choice}' not found.`)
    return
  }
  data = initialized.collections.exportLegacy(found)
  console.log(`  Exporting collection '${found.Name}' (${found.BeatmapMD5Hashes.filter(h => h).length} beatmaps)`)
}
```

</GuideSource>

`exportLegacy` returns a buffer in osu!stable's `collections.db` format. Write that buffer directly to the requested path.

<GuideSource source="examples/export-collection/index.js" :start-line="80" :end-line="80">

```js
writeFileSync(outputPath, data)
```

</GuideSource>

**API used:** [`init`](/api/generated/functions/init) · [`OsuFilesAPI#collections`](/api/generated/type-aliases/OsuFilesAPI#collections)

## Import a collection database

Merges a legacy `collections.db` file into the collections already stored in Realm.

[Full source](https://github.com/heyngra/osu-files/blob/main/examples/import-collection/index.js)

```sh
cd examples/import-collection
npm install
npm start
```

Import the legacy database in one call. Collections with new names are created; matching names receive any beatmap hashes they do not already contain.

<GuideSource source="examples/import-collection/index.js" :start-line="32" :end-line="38">

```js
console.log(`\nImporting ${legacyDbPath}...`)
const { imported, merged } = initialized.collections.importLegacy(legacyDbPath)
const total = initialized.collections.get.count()

console.log(`  Created:  ${imported} new collections`)
console.log(`  Merged:   ${merged} existing collections`)
console.log(`  Total:    ${total} collections in database`)
```

</GuideSource>

**API used:** [`init`](/api/generated/functions/init) · [`OsuFilesAPI#collections`](/api/generated/type-aliases/OsuFilesAPI#collections)

## Manage a collection

Adds beatmaps to a collection by online ID and removes them by list index.

[Full source](https://github.com/heyngra/osu-files/blob/main/examples/manage-collection/index.js)

```sh
cd examples/manage-collection
npm install
npm start
```

Collection queries return detached snapshots. Changes go through the collection module rather than mutating `col`.

<GuideSource source="examples/manage-collection/index.js" :start-line="50" :end-line="51">

```js
const col = osu.collections.get.byName(name).first()
if (!col) { console.log(`'${name}' not found.`); continue }
```

</GuideSource>

Collections store beatmap MD5 hashes, not online IDs. Look up the beatmap first, then add its MD5 hash to the selected collection.

<GuideSource source="examples/manage-collection/index.js" :start-line="83" :end-line="87">

```js
const beatmap = osu.beatmaps.get.byOnlineId(onlineId).first()
if (!beatmap) { console.log(`Beatmap ${onlineId} not found.`); continue }
if (!beatmap.MD5Hash) { console.log(`Beatmap ${onlineId} has no MD5Hash.`); continue }

osu.collections.addBeatmap(String(col.ID), beatmap.MD5Hash)
```

</GuideSource>

Removal uses the same MD5 hash. The local array is updated as well so the next prompt reflects the change without another query.

<GuideSource source="examples/manage-collection/index.js" :start-line="107" :end-line="108">

```js
osu.collections.removeBeatmap(String(col.ID), md5)
hashes.splice(idx, 1)
```

</GuideSource>
